  Pattern name      Unusually low rewards
  Rule              A reward is unusually low when it is below Q1 - 3 x IQR.
  Terms             Q1 is the first quartile and Q3 the third. IQR is Q3 - Q1, the spread of the
                    middle half.
  This run          Q1 is 1 and Q3 is 1, so the fence is 1.
  Flagged episodes  0004-simulator   Correct work rejected
                    0005-simulator   Incorrect work, failed
  Recorded          No error, timeout or refusal in these episodes.
  Details           2 of 12 usable 'reward' rewards are below the rest by the quartile rule (0004-
                    simulator 0, 0005-simulator 0; median 1, lower fence 1). None recorded an error,
                    timeout or refusal. A few lower rewards in a mostly higher pool can come from
                    model mistakes, sampling, time limits, refusals or infrastructure failures, or
                    from the tail of an ordinary spread. They can also come from a grader that
                    rejects valid work or a prompt that admits another reading. This is a reward
                    pattern, not a finding; reading these episodes beside higher ones is the next
                    step. 10 of 12 are 1 (95% Wilson interval 0.55 to 0.95 for its share, assuming
                    independent episodes); SD and skewness follow from this share. Grader inspection
                    labels: 0004-simulator rejected_valid, 0005-simulator legitimate. A label
                    describes its episode, not this pattern.
  Meaning           A pattern to read, not a finding. It changes no rate and no result.
  Minimum           nudi checks this only with 10 or more usable rewards.
